briefs: Baghdad moves to take over Kurdish oil exports.
A bus crash in the UAE kills 13 people.
A record toll from the summer heatwave.
Iran says a 4th tanker hit a mine
Gas blast collapses a restaurant; 10+ hurt.
A standoff in Cartagena drags on into the night.
A magnitude 5.3 quake near the Nepal–India border.
A car bomb wounds 23 people in Colombia.
Moscow's count of a night of drone attacks.
UN: partners or family kill five women an hour.
Bitcoin slips under $60,000 for the first time in months.
The speaker is removed by 112 votes to 37.
Rebels say their advance has halted.
An E-3A heads to Poland after the border incident.
England win the 2nd T20I by 8 wickets; series 1–1.
Davis Cup: Czechs reach the semi-finals.
Mbappé scores twice on UCL matchday five.
Inflation is “still too high”, the NY Fed chief says.
A public inquiry into the blackout opens for comment.
Data centres told to cut seven US-listed entities.
Manufacturing PMI at 53.7; composite at a 6-month low.
Five field goals, one walk-off, on Monday night.
Milwaukee finally win after thirteen straight losses.
Dylan Larkin debuts for Montreal in a 2–1 loss.
